In [[algebraic geometry]], given a [[morphism of schemes|morphism]] ''f'': ''X'' → ''S'' of [[scheme (mathematics)|schemes]], the '''cotangent sheaf''' on ''X'' is the [[sheaf of modules|sheaf of <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-modules]] <math>\Omega_{X/S}</math> that [[representable functor|represents]] (or classifies) ''S''-[[derivation (differential algebra)|derivations]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08RL|title = Section 17.27 (08RL): Modules of differentials|publisher=[[The Stacks project]]}}</ref> in the sense: for any <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-modules ''F'', there is an isomorphism
:<math>\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\Omega_{X/S}, F) = \operatorname{Der}_S(\mathcal{O}_X, F)</math>
that depends naturally on ''F''. In other words, the cotangent sheaf is characterized by the [[universal property]]: there is the differential <math>d: \mathcal{O}_X \to \Omega_{X/S}</math> such that any ''S''-derivation <math>D: \mathcal{O}_X \to F</math> factors as <math>D = \alpha \circ d</math> with some <math>\alpha: \Omega_{X/S} \to F</math>.

In the case ''X'' and ''S'' are affine schemes, the above definition means that <math>\Omega_{X/S}</math> is the module of [[Kähler differential]]s. The standard way to construct a cotangent sheaf (e.g., Hartshorne, Ch II. § 8) is through a diagonal morphism (which amounts to gluing modules of Kähler differentials on affine charts to get the globally defined cotangent sheaf). The [[dual module]] of the cotangent sheaf on a scheme ''X'' is called the '''tangent sheaf''' on ''X'' and is sometimes denoted by <math>\Theta_X</math>.<ref>In concise terms, this means:
:<math>\Theta_X \overset{\mathrm{def}} = \mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\Omega_X, \mathcal{O}_X) = \mathcal{D}er(\mathcal{O}_X).</math>
</ref>

There are two important [[exact sequence]]s:
#If ''S'' →''T'' is a morphism of schemes, then
#:<math>f^* \Omega_{S/T} \to \Omega_{X/T} \to \Omega_{X/S} \to 0.</math>
#If ''Z'' is a closed subscheme of ''X'' with [[ideal sheaf]] ''I'', then
#:<math>I/I^2 \to \Omega_{X/S} \otimes_{O_X} \mathcal{O}_Z \to \Omega_{Z/S} \to 0.</math><ref>{{harvnb|Hartshorne|1977|loc=Ch. II, Proposition 8.12.}}</ref><ref>https://mathoverflow.net/q/79956 as well as {{harv|Hartshorne|1977|loc=Ch. II, Theorem 8.17.}}</ref>

The cotangent sheaf is closely related to [[smooth variety|smoothness]] of a variety or scheme. For example, an algebraic variety is [[smooth variety|smooth]] of dimension ''n'' if and only if Ω<sub>''X''</sub> is a [[locally free sheaf]] of rank ''n''.<ref>{{harvnb|Hartshorne|1977|loc=Ch. II, Theorem 8.15.}}</ref>

== Construction through a diagonal morphism ==
{{See also|Cotangent bundle#Formal definition via diagonal morphism}}
Let <math>f: X \to S</math> be a morphism of schemes as in the introduction and Δ: ''X'' → ''X'' ×<sub>''S''</sub> ''X'' the diagonal morphism. Then the image of Δ is [[locally closed]]; i.e., closed in some open subset ''W'' of ''X'' ×<sub>''S''</sub> ''X'' (the image is closed if and only if ''f'' is [[separated morphism|separated]]). Let ''I'' be the ideal sheaf of Δ(''X'') in ''W''. One then puts:
:<math>\Omega_{X/S} = \Delta^* (I/I^2)</math>
and checks this sheaf of modules satisfies the required universal property of a cotangent sheaf (Hartshorne, Ch II. Remark 8.9.2). The construction shows in particular that the cotangent sheaf is [[quasi-coherent sheaf|quasi-coherent]]. It is coherent if ''S'' is [[Noetherian scheme|Noetherian]] and ''f'' is of finite type.

The above definition means that the cotangent sheaf on ''X'' is the restriction to ''X'' of the [[conormal sheaf]] to the diagonal embedding of ''X'' over ''S''.

{{See also|bundle of principal parts}}

== Relation to a tautological line bundle ==
{{main|Euler sequence}}

The cotangent sheaf on a projective space is related to the [[tautological line bundle]] ''O''(-1) by the following exact sequence: writing <math>\mathbf{P}^n_R</math> for the [[Proj_construction#Projective_n-space|projective space over a ring]] ''R'',
:<math>0 \to \Omega_{\mathbf{P}^n_R/R} \to \mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^n_R}(-1)^{\oplus(n+1)} \to \mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^n_R} \to 0.</math>

(See also [[Chern class#Complex projective space]].)

== Cotangent stack ==
For this notion, see § 1 of
:A. Beilinson and V. Drinfeld, Quantization of Hitchin’s integrable system and Hecke eigensheaves [http://www.math.uchicago.edu/~mitya/langlands/hitchin/BD-hitchin.pdf] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150105083234/http://www.math.uchicago.edu/~mitya/langlands/hitchin/BD-hitchin.pdf |date=2015-01-05 }}<ref>see also: § 3 of http://www.math.harvard.edu/~gaitsgde/grad_2009/SeminarNotes/Sept22(Dmodstack1).pdf</ref>
There, the cotangent stack on an [[algebraic stack]] ''X'' is defined as the [[relative Spec]] of the [[symmetric algebra]] of the tangent sheaf on ''X''. (Note: in general, if ''E'' is a [[locally free sheaf]] of finite rank, <math>\mathbf{Spec}(\operatorname{Sym}(\check{E}))</math> is the [[algebraic vector bundle]] corresponding to ''E''.{{Citation needed|date=June 2019}})

See also: [[Hitchin fibration]] (the cotangent stack of <math>\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)</math> is the total space of the Hitchin fibration.)
